sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

body.tldr: Randomly formed groups behave unlike independent regression clusters once a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The exact normalized Kneser operator yields a finite-sample design-variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order. A two-permutation martingale then gives centered design-based Gaussian inference under predictable-variation stabilization. The familiar equal-group CR2 statistic consistently estimates the independent-group term, so it is valid but conservative in the dense regime and ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible. When the sampling fraction vanishes, studentized normality holds without the birthday restriction \(N_n^2/n\to0\), but this replaces the comparator's Assumption 1 by statistic-specific predictable-QV stabilization and is therefore an assumption trade rather than a pure weakening. An enumerable eight-unit design verifies the factor-two variance excess. Most sharply, equal-observation Rademacher priors satisfy the exact reveal-filtration QV condition and yield deterministic dense schedule arrays with separated variance limits, proving that no one-realization statistic is uniformly ratio-consistent for exact variance. This impossibility already holds on the additive no-interference subclass and therefore transfers to arbitrary composition interference.

project_justification.gap: FuSamiiWang2026 defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws, which requires \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation loses first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while the fixed-cluster CR2 literature has no mechanism for restoring it.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so the exact causal variance can be decomposed by Johnson degree before treatment randomization is averaged out. This exposes a scalar sampling-fraction phase transition that whole-tuple coupling cannot see.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance and a schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder, proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale, obtains a centered martingale CLT, characterizes CR2 conservativeness and ratio consistency, verifies the exact software statistic and finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem by a filtration-specific predictable-QV calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 covers a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 prove asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase: replacing the birthday condition and Assumption 1 by statistic-specific predictable-QV stabilization is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, while the dense theorem retains the dependence their whole-tuple coupling removes. The positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic eigenspace architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies an explicit classical spectrum source, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform the complete-randomization component. \cite{Ohlsson1989} and \cite{Chao1997} inform the two-stage permutation-martingale route. Theorem 1 and Appendix A of \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explain CR2 working-model calibration under independent clusters; \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. Neither covers the random-partition correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} characterizes optimized conservative quadratic bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; they inform, but do not subsume, the proved equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound. That lower bound holds already on an additive no-interference subclass, so it transfers upward to the full arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias equals \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. The Rademacher variance limits are separated only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their limit gap is zero. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is only the benchmark at which the deterministic correction meets that bound, not a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results are restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
body.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, bounded-increment lemma, centered CLT conditional on predictable-variation stabilization, CR2 frontier, sparse reduction, software equality, eight-unit witness, Rademacher predictable-QV verification, and the resulting deterministic-diagonal all-statistic lower bound are theorem targets. The sparse studentization result trades the comparator's Assumption 1 and birthday condition for statistic-specific predictable-QV stabilization; shared boundedness remains in force, so this is not presented as a pure weakening. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\), holds on additive no-interference schedules, and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary composition interference. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish; when \(\rho>0\), no finite-sample conservativeness claim is made. Positive homogeneous conclusions are not asserted for variable group sizes.
